Can you write off your car? Only the part you can prove.
Say you drove twenty thousand kilometres this year. Twelve thousand were for your business.
Gas, insurance, repairs, licence: six thousand two hundred dollars for the year.
Sixty percent of that is three thousand, seven hundred and twenty. That's your deduction.
In our sixty-thousand-dollar Manitoba example, that saves about thirteen hundred dollars of tax and C-P-P.
But driving from home to your regular place of business? That's personal.
And that seventy-three cents a kilometre? That's for employer allowances. Self-employed people claim actual costs.
No logbook? The C-R-A can deny the claim. Date, destination, purpose, kilometres.
Keep one full year. After that, a three-month sample can work, if your driving stays similar.
Your car isn't the write-off. Your business kilometres are.
